description: Managing passwords, accounts, files, photos, backups, phone storage and screen time across personal devices and cloud services.
research_note: WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) when this researcher started and outbound fetches (including hn.algolia.com) were refused by the proxy, so no online sourcing was possible. All items are from prior knowledge and are labelled source_type=knowledge with empty source fields; searches_run lists the attempted queries.

items.title: Password reset loop on rarely used sites
items.problem: Every time you return to a site you use twice a year you can't remember the password, so you reset it, pick a new one, and forget that one too.
items.who: anyone with dozens of low-frequency accounts
items.workaround: browser autofill, reusing one password, sticky notes

items.title: Not knowing which email a login uses
items.problem: You know you have an account but not whether it was created with your personal, work or old university email, so the reset email never arrives.
items.workaround: trying each email in turn, searching inboxes for 'welcome' mails

items.title: Shared household logins get out of sync
items.problem: One partner changes the Netflix, Wi-Fi or utility password and the other is locked out; nobody knows the current one.
items.workaround: group chat scrollback, shared note, texting each other

items.title: Two-factor codes tied to an old phone
items.problem: After switching phones the authenticator app is gone and every 2FA-protected account has to be recovered one by one, sometimes with support tickets.
items.workaround: screenshots of recovery codes, SMS fallback, support tickets

items.title: Password manager mis-fills or saves the wrong site
items.problem: The manager offers three stale entries for one site, fills the username into the password box, or never prompts to save on some forms.
items.workaround: manual copy-paste, cleaning duplicates by hand

items.title: Site password rules reject generated passwords
items.problem: The generated 24-character password is refused for length or a banned symbol, forcing manual tweaking that isn't saved back to the manager.
items.workaround: edit the generated password, hope the manager updated it

items.title: Which accounts share a breached password
items.problem: A breach notice arrives for one site and you cannot easily tell which other accounts reuse the same or similar password.
items.workaround: guessing from memory, haveibeenpwned checks per email

items.title: Security questions with forgotten made-up answers
items.problem: Years ago you gave a joke answer for 'first pet' and now the bank or airline account is unrecoverable.

items.title: Nobody can access accounts if you die
items.problem: Partners and family have no way to reach photos, bank logins, domains and subscriptions if the account owner dies or is incapacitated.
items.workaround: a sealed envelope, a note in a drawer, nothing

items.title: Forgotten accounts on hundreds of sites
items.problem: Over 15 years you have signed up for hundreds of services; you have no list of them, and each one holds your name, email and often card details.
items.workaround: searching inbox for 'verify your email', ignoring it

items.title: Deleting an account requires a hidden process
items.problem: Closing an account means hunting through settings, emailing support or mailing a form, so the accounts just stay open.
items.who: anyone trying to reduce their footprint

items.title: Free trials that silently convert to paid
items.problem: A 7-day trial charges the card because nobody reminded you before the cutoff, and cancellation after the fact is refused.
items.workaround: calendar reminders, virtual cards, disputing charges

items.title: No single view of all recurring subscriptions
items.problem: Subscriptions are spread across App Store, Google Play, PayPal, cards and direct debits, so the true monthly total is unknown.

items.title: Losing access when a login is through a dead social account
items.problem: Accounts created with 'Sign in with Facebook/Twitter' become unreachable when that social account is deleted or suspended.
items.who: people who quit a social network

items.title: Old email address still used for recovery
items.problem: The recovery email on key accounts is an ISP or school address that no longer exists, discovered only at the moment of lockout.
items.workaround: auditing accounts one at a time after a scare

items.title: Family plan seats and who pays
items.problem: Family sharing for music, storage and streaming is split across several people's accounts and nobody knows who is on which plan or who is paying.
items.who: families and friend groups sharing plans

items.title: Thousands of near-duplicate photos
items.problem: Burst shots, screenshots and re-saved WhatsApp images bloat the library, and picking the best of ten near-identical frames by hand is tedious.
items.workaround: manual swiping in Photos, third-party duplicate finders

items.title: Photos scattered across phones, clouds and drives
items.problem: Pictures live in iCloud, Google Photos, an old laptop, WhatsApp exports and a partner's phone, with no single complete library.

items.title: Screenshots that are never revisited
items.problem: Hundreds of screenshots of recipes, addresses and memes sit in the camera roll, unsearchable and indistinguishable from real photos.

items.title: Can't find a specific old photo
items.problem: You know a photo exists ('the one of grandma at the lake') but cannot find it among 40,000 images without a date.

items.title: Shared event photos never get collected
items.problem: After a wedding or trip, photos are spread across a dozen phones and group chats and most are never pooled in one place at full quality.
items.who: friend groups, wedding guests, parents at school events
items.workaround: WhatsApp groups (compressed), shared albums someone forgets to invite people to

items.title: Photos from an ex or a bad period keep resurfacing
items.problem: Memories features and widgets show photos you'd rather not see, and hiding or bulk-removing a person is clumsy.
items.who: anyone after a breakup or loss

items.title: Scanned family prints lack dates and names
items.problem: Boxes of old prints get scanned but nobody records who is in them or when, so the context dies with the older relatives.

items.title: Videos silently eat most of the storage
items.problem: A handful of 4K videos take more space than years of photos, but the library doesn't make it obvious which clips are worth keeping.

items.title: Downloads folder is a landfill
items.problem: Every PDF, installer and attachment lands in Downloads and stays there for years; finding last month's invoice means sorting through hundreds of files.

items.title: Final_v2_FINAL(3).docx versioning chaos
items.problem: Multiple copies of a document with slightly different names exist on desktop, email and cloud, and nobody knows which is the latest.
items.workaround: naming conventions nobody follows, checking timestamps

items.title: Important documents buried in email attachments
items.problem: The lease, insurance policy or child's vaccination record exists only as an attachment in some email from years ago.
items.workaround: searching email, asking the sender again

items.title: Files split across three cloud drives
items.problem: Work uses OneDrive, personal uses Google Drive, old files are in Dropbox, and you cannot search all of them at once.
items.who: people with work and personal devices
items.workaround: remembering where things live, checking each one

items.title: Can't open old file formats
items.problem: Files from a decade ago (.pages, .wps, old camera RAW, WordPerfect) won't open on current software and the originals are irreplaceable.
items.workaround: online converters, keeping an old machine

items.title: Scanned receipts and forms are unsearchable images
items.problem: Photos of paper documents pile up with names like IMG_4521 and no text search, so retrieving one for taxes or warranty is slow.
items.workaround: scanner apps used inconsistently, a shoebox

items.title: Losing track of what was shared with whom
items.problem: Documents shared via cloud links years ago remain accessible to ex-colleagues, exes and strangers, and there is no easy audit.

items.title: Nobody actually tests their backups
items.problem: A backup exists in theory, but it has never been restored, and the failure is discovered only when the drive dies.

items.title: Phone backup silently stopped months ago
items.problem: iCloud or Google backup failed quietly because storage was full, and the last good backup turns out to be six months old.
items.workaround: noticing the warning banner, paying for storage

items.title: Chat history lost when switching platforms
items.problem: Years of WhatsApp or iMessage history do not move between Android and iPhone, or are lost when a backup is tied to the old cloud.

items.title: External backup drive is out of date
items.problem: The backup drive in the drawer was last plugged in over a year ago because there is no nudge to do it.
items.who: people with a manual backup habit

items.title: Cloud account suspension would take everything
items.problem: All photos, email and documents sit in one Google or Apple account; a false-positive suspension or lost login would erase digital life.
items.workaround: takeout exports done once, never repeated

items.title: No inventory of what needs backing up
items.problem: Data lives on a phone, laptop, two USB sticks, a game console and a NAS, and nobody has a list of what is where and what is protected.

items.title: 'Storage almost full' at the worst moment
items.problem: The phone refuses to take a photo or update because storage is full, and clearing space in the moment means deleting things blindly.
items.workaround: deleting apps and videos in a panic, 'offload' features

items.title: Mystery 'Other' or 'System' storage
items.problem: Tens of gigabytes are labelled Other/System with no way to see what they are or safely remove them.

items.title: Messaging app media fills the phone
items.problem: Auto-downloaded group-chat videos and forwarded memes quietly consume gigabytes, with cleanup buried deep in settings.

items.title: Unused apps hog space and permissions
items.problem: Dozens of apps opened once still take space, send notifications and hold location and contacts permissions.

items.title: Old devices with data still on them
items.problem: Retired phones and laptops sit in a drawer with photos and logins on them, too risky to donate and too much work to wipe properly.

items.title: Battery dying earlier than expected each day
items.problem: Some app drains the battery in the background and identifying the culprit from the OS battery screen is confusing.

items.title: Screen time limits are trivially bypassed
items.problem: Built-in limits are dismissed with 'ignore for today' or 'one more minute', so they stop working within a week.
items.who: adults trying to cut phone use
items.workaround: grayscale mode, deleting apps, dumb phone

items.title: Opening the phone for one thing, losing 20 minutes
items.problem: You unlock to check the weather, get pulled into a feed, and forget what you came for.

items.title: Doomscrolling in bed delays sleep
items.problem: Late-night scrolling pushes bedtime back and the phone is also the alarm, so it can't simply be left in another room.

items.title: Screen-time reports don't distinguish useful from wasteful use
items.problem: Weekly reports lump maps, reading and work chat together with feeds, making the number meaningless and easy to ignore.

items.title: Kids' screen limits negotiated per device
items.problem: Children's time is spread across tablet, console, TV and a friend's phone, and limits set on one device don't count the others.
items.workaround: verbal rules, separate parental controls per device

items.title: Notification overload from every app
items.problem: Dozens of apps send promotional pings, so real messages are buried and the reflex is to check the phone constantly.
items.workaround: muting apps one by one, Do Not Disturb

items.title: Data broker profiles keep reappearing
items.problem: Personal address and phone number show up on people-search sites, and removal requests have to be repeated every few months.

items.title: Old posts and accounts embarrass you years later
items.problem: Content from teenage years on forums and social media is still findable by employers and dates, and cleanup is per-post.

items.title: Wi-Fi password sharing with guests
items.problem: Guests ask for the Wi-Fi and the router password is a 20-character string on a sticker in a cupboard.
items.workaround: reading it aloud, photographing the sticker, QR code taped up
